summary: rb_ger is at the memory floor: the baseline (loop-free, 16 bytes per lane, one 1 KB-contiguous wave per workgroup) has headroom 0.89-0.90 against the copy model (268 MB read + 268 MB written in 94 us, 5.7 TB/s), and every element of A must be read and written exactly once, so 1.5x is out of reach; x (32 KB) is re-read per column but from cache. The shipped state 119155ff4a28c113 only shortens the per-wave latency chain in the prologue: amdclang makes four sequential scalar-load round trips (alpha, m, pointers, y[col]) before the vector loads are issued; here all kernargs are fetched by two scalar loads issued together with one wait, and the y[col] load is in flight together with the x/A global_load_dwordx4 (its lgkmcnt wait and the res_y multiply moved after the vector loads, duplicated into the tail path). Bit-identical arithmetic, battery 77/77, 1.016x over the baseline (CI 1.0125-1.0182, 240 pairs). No source state was made.

friction: The session opened with tag `best` pointing at f7bf704e9ce7c4a5, an older copy of the baseline source state (control 0.997), while `baseline` was a fresh unverified id d93b3d2c37dcb0e6: the earlier coarsen states hang off the old id, and list_states does not show their coarsen factors (action 'coarsen' with empty note), so I could not tell which factor gave 1.006 / 0.97 / 0.92.

No transform for 'merge the kernarg scalar loads into one round trip' or 'sink an lgkmcnt wait past independent vector loads across a branch': both were done by hand and required duplicating the multiply into the tail path because the fast path and tail path are split by exec masks.

The edit that sank the wait across a branch was not run through static_check explicitly by me (check accepted it, which implies it passed); a pending scalar load across a conditional branch was accepted without comment, which is right but worth stating in the skill.
lessons: rb_ger (rank-1 update, 8192x8192 f32): the loop-free 16-bytes-per-lane, block-64 amdclang build runs at 5.7 TB/s, headroom 0.89-0.90 against the copy model: at the memory floor. Each A element is touched once (one read, one write); nothing to save in bytes.

In a loop-free one-wave-per-workgroup kernel (262144 waves of ~45 instructions), putting the last scalar load (y[col], whose address depends on a kernarg) in flight together with the vector loads instead of waiting for it first gave 1.015x (CI 1.012-1.017, 240 pairs), bit-identical. This is the only prologue change that measured.

Merging the three sequential kernarg s_load+wait round trips (alpha, m, pointers) into two loads issued together with one wait added only +0.1% (1.0149 -> 1.016): kernarg loads are cache hits and their round trips are cheap; not worth doing alone.
coarsen factor 2 on the improved loop-free state: 0.985 against it (CI 0.980-0.989). Consistent with the note that coarsen does not pay on loop-free 16-byte-per-lane kernels.

session.final:
`rb_ger` is at the memory floor, so the 1.5x target is out of reach; the best verified state is `119155ff4a28c113` at 1.016x over the baseline (95% CI 1.0125–1.0182, 240 pairs, battery 77/77).

- **Why 1.5x is out of reach:** the baseline already moves 268 MB read plus 268 MB written in 94 µs (5.7 TB/s), a headroom of 0.89–0.90 against the copy model. Every element of `A` is read and written exactly once, so there are no bytes to save.
- **What the shipped state changes:** only the per-wave prologue.
  - The `y[col]` scalar load is now in flight together with the `x`/`A` vector loads instead of being waited for first. This is the edit that measured: 1.015x on its own (`f8d1294bd126d8d0`).
  - The kernel arguments come in through two scalar loads issued together with one wait, instead of three sequential round trips. This added only about 0.1%, which is within noise.
- **What did not pay:** `coarsen` factor 2 on top of the best state was a loss, 0.985 against it (CI 0.980–0.989).

The margin is thin: the harness re-verifies with two fresh 240-pair timings and takes the lower, and the CI's lower bound sits just above the 1.01 noise floor. I stopped after about five minutes and four timed candidates.

The report is recorded at `.agc/sessions/rb_ger-65bf7e9921/report.json`.
